title: Office Administrator
description:
We are currently recruiting for an Office Administrator on behalf of an accountancy firm based in Lincoln. The role is available on either a full-time or part-time basis.

Given the nature of the business, previous experience within an accountancy practice or professional services environment is essential.

Responsibilities:
- Accurately maintain the current system for managing client records which includes scanning relevant documents, ready for the chargeable team to use and contacting the clients when they are ready for collection.
- Monitor and communicate with Directors regarding client meetings and check if client records can be returned at meetings.
- Understand the functions of the different departments within the firm and what they require in accessing electronic records.
- Assist with the post system as required.
- Assist in the maintenance of other databases for the firm keeping client details up to date.
- Preparation and management of key documents such as engagement letters.
- Other general office duties as required to include answering the telephone, greeting clients and taking card payments as part of the administrative team.
- Contacting clients when required to inform them of upcoming deadlines to help with the tax and accounts departments.
- Maintaining systems and monitoring deadlines as required.
- Ability to cover other admin functions as required.
- Assistance with other admin tasks as directed by admin manager.

Requirements:
- Strong organisational skills with an eye for detail.
- Ability to multitask and prioritise tasks effectively.
- High level of professionalism and discretion.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Previous experience within an accountancy firm or professional services environment (essential).

Benefits:
- Competitive salary in line with market rate
- Company pension scheme
- Open to both full-time or part-time applicants
- Discounted City Centre parking
- Flexibility in working hours
- 25 days annual leave Bank Holidays Birthday off
- Regular social events
- Supportive team culture
- Central office location, close to transport links

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Location: Office-based, PE9
Contract: Fixed Term until 30 April 2027 (6 months)
Start Date: ASAP
Hours: Negotiable, minimum 25 hours per week across at least 4 days (Monday to Friday). Maximum 35 hours per week across 5 days.

About the Role

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Office Administrator with a bookkeeping background to join a busy and friendly organisation on a fixed-term basis. This varied role will support multiple business areas, including administration, hospitality, retail, and operational functions, while providing excellent service to members, visitors, and colleagues.

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the organisation's migration to Xero and will contribute to the smooth day-to-day running of the office.

- Identify and recommend process improvements to increase efficiency across the organisation.

- Handle general enquiries from members and visitors in a professional and friendly manner.
- Manage bookings and reservations as required.
- Support various departments with administrative tasks.
- Provide temporary cover within the retail environment when required (subject to training).

Skills & Experience Required
- Previous experience in an office administration role.
- Bookkeeping experience with a strong working knowledge of Xero.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word and Excel.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and work independently.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and process improvement.
- Professional and customer-focused attitude.

Benefits
- Fixed-term contract until 30 April 2027.
- Potential opportunity for the role to become permanent.
- Bank Holidays plus 20 days annual leave (pro rata).
- Flexible working hours within agreed requirements.
- Varied and interesting role within a supportive team environment.

title: Data Protection Coordinator
description:
Data Protection Coordinator

Hybrid UK £28,000 + Bonus

Shape the Future of Data Privacy

An established and growing UK organisation is looking for a Data Protection Coordinator to play a key role in embedding privacy and data protection best practice across the business. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a solid understanding of UK GDPR who wants to develop their career within a collaborative environment where compliance, security and governance are highly valued.

Working closely with teams across IT, Legal, HR and the wider business, you'll help ensure personal data is managed responsibly, compliance obligations are met, and privacy considerations are built into everyday operations.

What You'll Be Doing
- Supporting the organisation's data protection and privacy programme.
- Managing and coordinating Data Subject Rights Requests (DSARs), including Subject Access Requests and Right to Erasure requests.
- Assisting teams with Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs).
- Maintaining Records of Processing Activities (ROPA).
- Supporting investigations into data protection incidents and personal data breaches.
- Assisting with regulatory reporting requirements where necessary.
- Reviewing privacy implications of projects, systems and third-party suppliers.
- Supporting supplier due diligence and Data Processing Agreement reviews.
- Contributing to third-party privacy risk assessments.
- Developing and maintaining privacy policies, procedures and guidance.
- Coordinating employee awareness and data protection training initiatives.
- Monitoring changes in data protection legislation and regulatory guidance.
- Supporting internal and external compliance audits.
- Producing compliance reporting and management information.

What We're Looking For

You may already be working as a Data Protection Coordinator, Privacy Administrator, Compliance Coordinator or Governance professional and be looking for your next challenge.

You'll ideally bring:
- Experience working with UK GDPR and Data Protection legislation.
- Knowledge of managing Data Subject Rights Requests (DSARs).
- Understanding of DPIAs and privacy risk assessments.
- Experience maintaining Records of Processing Activities (ROPA).
- Knowledge of personal data incident management and breach response.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills with great attention to detail.
- A proactive approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

What's On Offer
- Salary of £28,000
- Quarterly performance-related bonus
- Hybrid working arrangement
- Comprehensive benefits package
- Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives
- Career development within a supportive and collaborative team
- Opportunity to gain broad exposure across privacy, compliance and governance disciplines.

Apply Today

If you're passionate about privacy, governance and helping organisations build strong data protection practices, we'd love to hear from you. This is a fantastic opportunity to join a forward-thinking business where your contribution will directly support compliance, risk management and operational excellence.

title: Trainee Legal Secretary
description:
Trainee Legal Secretary

Spalding

We are delighted to be working with a highly regarded national law firm on the appointment of a Trainee Float Team Legal Secretary to join their busy Spalding office.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to begin or develop their career within the legal sector, offering the chance to gain valuable experience across a variety of legal departments within an established and respected firm.

The Opportunity

If you enjoy variety, like staying busy and are keen to learn, this could be the perfect role for you.

As a Trainee Float Team Legal Secretary, you will spend time supporting different legal departments across the office, providing essential secretarial and administrative assistance to fee earners and wider teams. With exposure to different areas of law, no two days will be the same, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad skill set and gain an insight into how a busy legal practice operates.

You will play an important role in helping the teams run efficiently, ensuring that administrative tasks are completed accurately and that clients receive a professional and helpful service.

Key Responsibilities

Your duties will include:
- Providing secretarial and administrative support across a range of legal departments
- Preparing, formatting and amending correspondence and legal documents
- Managing incoming and outgoing communications, including telephone calls and emails
- Assisting with document management, filing and maintaining accurate records
- Supporting diary management, appointments and general departmental administration
- Helping to ensure client information and documentation are handled professionally and confidentially
- Working collaboratively with solicitors, fee earners and colleagues across the office
- Learning new processes and adapting to the requirements of different teams

About You

We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and proactive individual who is keen to learn and enjoys working in a varied, fast-paced environment.

You will ideally have:
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- A professional and friendly telephone manner
- Good IT skills and confidence using Microsoft Office
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively
- A flexible approach and the willingness to support different teams as required
- A positive attitude, eagerness to learn and a genuine interest in developing a career within the legal sector
- The ability to work well both independently and as part of a team

Previous legal secretarial experience would be beneficial, but a willingness to learn, a positive attitude and a strong work ethic are equally important.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a fantastic opportunity to gain hands-on experience within a professional legal environment while developing the skills and confidence needed to build a career in legal administration.

The float team structure offers exposure to multiple legal departments, allowing you to broaden your knowledge, learn from experienced professionals and discover different areas of the legal sector.

If you are looking for a role that offers variety, development and the opportunity to become a valued member of a busy team, this could be an excellent next step.

Interested?

If you are organised, enthusiastic and looking for an opportunity to start or develop your career as a Legal Secretary in Spalding, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

title: Patient Administrator
company: Lincolnshire Community Health Service NHS Trust

description: Do you have excellent communication and administration skills with recent experience of working in a busy office environment where no two days are the same? Are you a proficient Microsoft Office and IT user? If you're looking for a rewarding administrative role where you can make a positive difference to people's experience of the NHS, then joining our patient admin services team and working alongside our community nursing and specialist services colleagues could be right for you. We're looking for experienced administrators who can transfer their skills to the NHS, ensuring that our community clinicians and patients are always supported with expert admin help. You should be willing and available to work on a rota basis usually between 0800-17:00hrs Monday to Friday. Roles in Lincoln/Skegness & Mablethorpe - other bases to be confirmed but can potentially work from any of our offices countywide Following policies, procedures and quality standards, to provide a professional and efficient administrative service which enables our clinical teams to focus on delivering patient care. To be the first person our patients see when they arrive at the health clinic and ensure a welcoming environment. To communicate in a timely, sensitive and empathetic manner with patients and clients either verbally or non-verbally, ensuring accurate details are recorded and either actioned or passed in a timely manner to the responsible person/team. To support our clinical teams to ensure they have enough stock, paperwork and equipment to complete their day to day tasks. Provide a range of administrative functions, which may include producing letters, processing patient referrals, scanning, photocopying, taking minutes, booking rooms, sorting post and other office/administration duties. Welcome our patient as they arrive at the reception desks of the health clinic and ensure their arrival is logged on our patient information system Monitor voicemails and respond to enquiries from patients and clients, including handling potentially difficult calls, in a professional manner, assessing the urgency, taking messages and passing to the relevant person where necessary. Book, amend or cancel patient appointments, by telephone or face to face, ensuring all records are updated and patients and clients are informed. Advise patients on access to and use of services. Maintain accurate patient records using both computer and paper. Receive, record, transmit, store and retrieve information from paper or electronic records and databases.
